key_insight: White matter hyperintensities showed stronger associations with poorer verbal memory in non-Hispanic African American than non-Hispanic White older adults in two of three cohorts, with differences localized to specific white matter regions.
clinical_relevance: Spatially resolved white matter measures may help characterize vascular contributions to cognitive aging, but these findings do not establish clinical utility or race-based care recommendations.
method: Mapped white matter hyperintensities by depth and brain lobe across three independent cohorts.
Used cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses plus generalized random forests.
Adjusted for cohort-specific Alzheimer’s biomarkers, vascular risks, structural imaging measures and APOE genotype.
evidence_signal: Among 5,187 cognitively unimpaired older adults, group differences appeared in EHBS and a 34-center cohort but were not detected in the third cohort; implicated regions also differed between cohorts.
watch_item: Observational associations and inconsistent replication limit causal interpretation; racial categories should not be treated as biological mechanisms.
paper_title: Spatially localized racial differences in the association between white matter hyperintensities and verbal memory in cognitively unimpaired adults
